requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The change edits `TypeCollector` so that bad key layouts no longer crash the analyzer. A member whose key kind (int vs. string) doesn't match the others is now skipped after MsgPack005 is reported (lines 1008, 1148). A duplicate int or string key no longer causes a second `Dictionary.Add` that throws; the first member wins (lines 1023-1026, 1039-1042, 1163-1166, 1179-1182). It adds analyzer tests for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types, two execution tests, and a README section on opting out of source generation.
story.why: The issue says the analyzer stops working for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types since 3.1.1. The fix implies the cause was an unhandled exception from duplicate-key `Add` calls aborting analysis. The diff does not explain why that would only show up for suppressed types. One new test (`DuplicateKeysAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailureForGeneratedTypes`) shows the same crash path also applies to normal generated types. No code path that depends on `SuppressSourceGeneration` was changed.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section that documents analyzer behavior. It lists MsgPack012 as enforced, but no test covers that.
The `continue` after the mixed-key diagnostic and the duplicate-key guards change behavior for all `[MessagePackObject]` types, not only suppressed ones.
Execution tests check run-time round-tripping and that no generated formatter exists, which is generator/runtime behavior rather than analyzer behavior.
story.confidence_overview: High confidence that the edits remove an `ArgumentException` on duplicate keys. Medium-to-low confidence that this is the root cause of the reported regression: nothing in the visible diff is specific to `SuppressSourceGeneration`, and there is no evidence the new tests failed before the fix. The README claims are partly untested.

It does not exercise cited lines 1145-1149 (the field loop) at all, nor does it test the !isIntKey && stringKey == null case (and in the property loop at line 1028, else if (stringKey is not null) already prevented dereferencing a null stringKey).

Claim C4 disputed: After listing MsgPack004, MsgPack015, MsgPack003, and duplicate/mixed keys (MsgPack005), the claim asserts that nothing in the diff shows these tests failed before the fix. That is false for all three MsgPack005 tests (lines 80-144): TypeCollector.cs lines 1008, 1019, 1023-1026, and 1039-1042 directly show that before this fix, duplicate int/string keys threw ArgumentException from Dictionary.Add and mixed keys fell through to intKey!.Value and threw InvalidOperationException, crashing the analyzer.

Nothing in the diff ties the fix to `SuppressSourceGeneration`. The duplicate-key crash also applies to generated types (per the ForGeneratedTypes test). If 3.1.1 introduced a separate early exit or filter for suppressed types, this change does not touch it, and the reported regression may remain for valid-but-otherwise-flawed suppressed types. Root cause is not demonstrated.

`continue` skips the rest of the member processing for mixed-key members. Any later per-member diagnostics (for example the member-type MsgPack003 check or formatter-attribute handling below line 1045) will no longer be reported for that member.
For duplicate keys the second member is silently dropped from the model. If the generator still emits code despite the MsgPack005 error, the emitted formatter would omit that member rather than fail.
The README says MsgPack012 (accessibility) is still enforced for suppressed types, but no test verifies this. User-facing documentation claims behavior that is not covered by the tests.

When a duplicate string key is encountered on a property (line 1035) or field (line 1175), new MemberSerializationInfo(..., hiddenIntKey++, ...) still increments hiddenIntKey before the new !stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey) guard at lines 1039/1179 skips adding the duplicate member. Any subsequent valid string-keyed member on that type receives a non-contiguous synthetic IntKey (e.g., 0 then 2 when stringMembers.Count is 2), breaking the 0..Count-1 invariant if downstream generator code runs on invalid source in the IDE.
